backend: use unaligned PRG output for 32-bit value (#41)

layered_bucket_into_acc draws the per-layer cyclic-shift coin into a
stack uint32_t. PRG::random_data requires its destination to be
16-byte aligned, but a uint32_t object is not guaranteed to satisfy
that alignment, and Debug builds abort on emp-tool's alignment assert.

Use PRG::random_data_unaligned for this 4-byte draw.

Rewrite emp-ag2pc onto the no-Shape emp-tool: one public handle AG2PCCtx
replaces the object/stream two-mode split, the global emp::Backend path, and the
public Shape / SecureValue<Shape> layer. The authenticated-garbling pass
executor (the five passes over LambdaState) is preserved byte-for-byte.

AG2PCCtx (frontend/ag2pc_ctx.h) IS a BooleanContext (Wire = a bare uint32_t id;
no refcount, no singleton) and owns the crypto + executor + typed I/O. Internals
split into AG2PCProtocol (backend/protocol.h, crypto core: process_inputs /
decode / public_wires) and AG2PCExecutor (backend/executor.h, runs a
BooleanProgram or a live body source through the passes; hosts the per-pass
body-replay template).

Values are the emp-tool *_T<AG2PCCtx> types (UInt/Int/Float/Bits/Bit). Three
execution strategies share the passes: direct/chunked (operators record into a
chunk, flushed at reveal/checkpoint), compiled replay (ctx.run(circuit, ...)),
and live body replay (ctx.run_body(body, ...)); run/run_body require materialized
args (cross-mode mixing deferred). Wire liveness is explicit: checkpoint(keep...)
prunes carried state, reveal(v, recipient, keep...) flushes keeping v + keep,
stale ids error loudly. Eager input<T> plus a multi-owner input_batch() builder
(one process_inputs phase). ctx.run_program<RetV> is the typed raw-program escape
hatch (Bits_T for AES/SHA, never UInt>64). num_and() totals garbled ANDs across
all strategies.

The direct-chunk planner (DCE + canonical compaction + stale-operand detection)
is a pure, network-free ag2pc_detail::plan_flush, unit-tested by test_flush_plan.

program_replay / body_replay_equiv (byte-identical transcript gate) /
aes_sha_builtin (aes128 + sha256_256 .empbc vs a ClearCtx oracle). The run helper

ag2pc: frontend-first execution -- one streaming engine, three circuit sources

AG2PC circuits are written with the emp-tool frontend and executed through a
single streaming engine (LambdaRunner::run_engine_), driven by a "circuit
source": a replay callback that emits the circuit under the installed phase
backend and returns packed output wire ids. Three sources share the engine:

  - frontend body      run<Ins...>(inputs, body)        -> frontend::run(body, args)
  - compiled circuit   run_compiled<Ins...>(tc, inputs) -> frontend::run(tc, args)
  - legacy flat lambda run_circuit(in_wires, n_out, lambda)

A compiled circuit (frontend::compile -> TypedCircuit) is replayed by walking its
recorded BooleanProgram via frontend::run(tc, LambdaWire args): it issues the same
backend gate calls a body would, so it needs no separate materialized crypto.
This removes the BooleanProgram -> WireGraph frontend lowering entirely
(ag2pc_frontend.h / ag2pc::lower / ag2pc::compute deleted); WireGraph now serves
only the legacy/direct recorder.

LambdaRunner internals are factored into a clean source/engine boundary:
prepare_typed_inputs_, make_frontend_body_replay_, make_compiled_frontend_replay_,
make_flat_lambda_replay_, pack_output_ids_, run_engine_.

Streaming memory is linear in #AND gates + live width: a liveness pre-pass plus a
slot-reuse map (phys) recycle XOR/NOT fabric, so the per-wire crypto arrays no
longer grow with total wires (SHA-256 x50 peakRSS ~984MB -> ~662MB).

The frontend body source reuses emp-tool's pure-circuit contract
(circuit_fn_traits): prvalue args, return-by-value; lvalue-ref / reference-return /
non-circuit bodies are rejected with a single diagnostic (the contract trait is
instantiated once and output packing is guarded by if constexpr, so a bad body no
longer also emits a pack_wires(invalid_circuit_fn) error).

emp-ag2pc.h exposes LambdaRunner; lambda_circuit_types.h is intentionally left out
of the umbrella (its LambdaWire aliases collide with ag2pc_circuit_types.h).

Constant subtlety: frontend::compile dedupes CONST0/CONST1, so a compiled
circuit's gate stream/transcript may differ from the equivalent body replay; both
are correct KRRW. Equivalence for the compiled path is semantic/oracle, not
byte-identical transcript -- test_wire_equiv asserts byte equality only between
the two streaming front-doors, and oracle equality for the compiled path.

Tests: frontend compile/run over the direct recorder (test_frontend{,_chain,_typed}),
compiled via run_compiled (test_frontend_materialized, test_lambda_compiled),
streaming body (test_lambda_frontend), lambda AES/SHA-256 (test_lambda_{aes,sha256}),
and a wire-equivalence guard (test_wire_equiv). Full ctest: 17/17.

without changing protocol behavior. All 8 local tests + SHA x 200
stress run stay GOOD.

    operation on abit1 (with io_abit1) and abit2 (with io_abit2)
    concurrently. Replaces the three near-identical
    pool->enqueue pair sites in ~TriplePool (end+flush), init_abit_
    (begin+flush), and flush_cot_check (end+flush+begin) -- each
    becomes a single one-line call.

ag2pc_backend.h
  - carry_load_ / carry_store_ helpers factor the per-wire copy
    between SecureWires[i] and CarriedState. gather_carried_ and
    stash_carried_ shrink to a one-liner per element and stop
    duplicating the is_eval branch on label0 vs eval_label.

2pc.h
  - Drop the auto WIRE/LABEL/EVAL = [&](int w) { return ctx.WIRE(w); }
    lambdas that were defined at the top of collect_masks,
    garble_and_ship, evaluate, check_cgamma, and gather_outputs
    (4 sites, ~10 lambda definitions total). Call sites now use
    ctx.WIRE(w) / ctx.LABEL(w) / ctx.EVAL(w) directly; the lambdas
    were pure forwarders to those ComputeCtx methods.
  - Unify the per-chunk staging struct (was GarbleChunk { ...; int
    nfilled; } in garble_and_ship and EvalChunk { ...; int len; } in
    evaluate). Both now use a single StreamChunk { BlockVec G;
    vector<unsigned char> b; int n; } declared on C2PC. The
    pool-thread role (sender vs receiver) still differs and stays
    inlined per function.
  - recompute_share(g, ctx) static helper: the "NOT copies WIRE, XOR
    xor_share-s WIRE" line shows up in collect_masks,
    garble_and_ship, evaluate, and both branches of check_cgamma --
    every gate-walk needs to refresh the fabric-recycled XOR/NOT
    share before reading an AND that consumes it. One named helper
    instead of five inline copies.
  - propagate_mask(g, Lambda) static helper: the "NOT flips mask,
    XOR XORs mask" linear propagation shared by evaluate's non-AND
    branch and the garbler-side of check_cgamma (the garbler doesn't
    run evaluate but still needs Λ on intermediate wires before its

ag2pc: batched process_inputs (KRRW Fig.3) -- whole input phase in ~1 RTT

Replace the per-owner process_input loop with a single batched
process_inputs(owners, bits_per_owner) call that handles both parties'
input wires together. Per chunk the input phase is now one protocol
invocation (~1 RTT on the wire) regardless of owner count, instead of
the old 1.5 RTT * K-owners sequential.

Structure (KRRW Fig.3 input phase):

  1. fpre->draw mints all n_total authenticated lambda-shares in one
     COT batch.
  2. Garbler samples m_{w,0} for every wire.
  3. Authenticated share open + Gamma reveal, folded into ONE duplex
     round. Each party ships, in parallel on send_io / recv_io:
        - lambda^self bits for ALL wires        (n_total bytes)
        - Hash(MAC for those wires)             (DIGEST_SIZE bytes)
        - x_w bits for wires this party owns    (n_owned bytes)
     Recipient verifies the MAC hash against expected
     KEY ^ bit*Delta from its own wire_bundle.key + Delta; aborts on
     mismatch. Both then compute Gamma_w = lambda^A ^ lambda^B ^ x_w
     locally for every wire. The MAC hash matches the decode-side
     authenticator pattern.
  4. Garbler ships m_{w,Gamma_w} = label0 ^ Gamma_w*Delta for all
     wires (one-way).

Why fold (3) and the Gamma-ship into one round: in KRRW Fig.3 the
share Open and the Gamma reveal are written as separate steps, but
the Open's MAC verification only cares that the shipped share bits
match the corresponding MACs; folding the owner's x bits into the
same packet doesn't weaken that. The Gamma value itself is bound by
the chunk-end c_gamma check on downstream AND gates, so it doesn't
need a per-bit authenticator at this layer (same argument we used for
the decode-side authenticator landing in the prior commit).

ag2pc: pipeline per-chunk garble send and evaluate recv against compute

Both garble_and_ship (P2) and p1_evaluate (P1) stream the garbled-table
chunks across a single socket. The old code did the blocking
send/flush (resp. recv) inline in the per-AND compute loop, so each

so the IO call runs on a pool thread while compute proceeds on the

ag2pc: RAII-tracked smart checkpoint_keep_all via 4-byte AG2PCWire carrier

The previous explicit checkpoint_ag2pc(keep, n) forced the user to enumerate
every still-live wire (and silently corrupted state if any live wire was
omitted). Its conservative successor checkpoint_ag2pc_keep_all() carried every
recorder-known wire, so wires whose Bit handles had gone out of scope were
still kept — useful, but didn't actually drop {Bit b;}-style dead wires.

This replaces the int-id-in-block carrier with a 4-byte AG2PCWire struct that
pins a per-id refcount on copy/destruct via a backend singleton. The recorder
now stores per-wire metadata in flat arrays (refcount + op + parents) indexed
by slot id, with a free-list stack returning dead slots for reuse at chunk
boundaries. Cross-chunk authenticated state lives in a sparse carried_ map
keyed by recorder id. checkpoint_ag2pc_keep_all() walks the alive set
(refcount > 0), does backward reachability over the chunk's gate log
(dead branches are pruned — the protocol never pays for them), runs the
protocol, stashes carried_ for every alive id that surfaces in the chunk's
WireGraph, and pushes dead slots onto the free list. The user gets RAII
liveness ({ Bit b; } drops b automatically) with no stale-handle footgun.

The half-gate leaky-AND (Pi_LaAND, eprint 2018/578 Fig. 5) ran as a
parallel C-precompute phase, then a sender/receiver exchange that shared

lambdas that share only the read-only aShares:

    S = H(K) ^ E ^ (K[r]^M[r]) ^ x*C ^ r*Delta into its own Sout.

the only cross-thread value, so the two threads need no lock or handoff.
